QUOTE: "If the symbol is not defined, `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE` renames the member. If it is defined, the macro expands to the bare member name." and "The guard only constrains outside users. Any external code that defines `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` before including the headers gets the same access"
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that defining the symbol yields bare member names (library, sample programs, external code that defines it), while ordinary consumers of the public headers get `private_`-renamed names.
